name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad
positioning: The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad, a Manhattan hotel at West 28th Street and Broadway with three José Andrés venues, a Club lounge on the 36th floor and a subterranean spa
best_for: Travelers who want to dine at José Andrés venues without leaving the hotel
Guests who want a base within reach of Madison Square Park and the Empire State Building

facts.text: The hotel is on the corner of West 28th Street and Broadway.
Nearby attractions include Madison Square Park, the Flatiron Building, the Empire State Building, Bryant Park, Hudson Yards and the High Line.
Zaytinya, the hotel's all-day restaurant, serves mezze inspired by Turkish, Greek and Lebanese cuisines.
Nubeluz is a rooftop cocktail bar by José Andrés, designed by Martin Brudzinski.
The Tour de José is a private guided evening through Zaytinya, Bazaar Bar, Bazaar Meat and Nubeluz.
The spa offers facials and massages by Augustinus Bader, Dr. Dennis Gross and ESPA.
Bathrooms are finished in terrazzo marble and stocked with Diptyque amenities.
Rooms have oversized windows with views of New York City.
The Penthouse Residences have full kitchens and access to The Ritz-Carlton Club Lounge.
Children staying as Ritz Kids get a special check-in experience, custom amenities and itineraries from the concierge team.
Condé Nast Traveler's review says each room has a stand-alone soaking tub and steam shower.

highlights.text: The hotel was conceived as a pillar of the city's historic floral district, and its decor and design draw inspiration from nature.
The Ritz-Carlton Club lounge is on the 36th floor of the building.
Bazaar Meat is a steakhouse by chef José Andrés where wood-fired cooking is at the heart of the menu.
The Ritz-Carlton Spa is a subterranean space with separate relaxation lounges, saunas and steam rooms.
The Ritz-Carlton Suite has two bedrooms, a dining area, a media room and a private wellness space.

considerations.text: Club lounge access requires an upgraded booking of a Club Level guestroom or suite.
Reservations are required for Nubeluz and The Bazaar by José Andrés.
WhataHotel notes a busy Midtown Manhattan location with urban noise levels.
